Predicting Premier League home wins

ISC 4241 final project - logistic regression vs decision trees and random forests, 10-fold chronological cross-validation, collinearity and residual diagnostics, one untouched test season.

65.6%Selected model, 2024-25 test accuracy
62.6%Baseline logistic (original 5-game form)
58.7%Always "not a home win"
66.4%Bookmakers (benchmark only)

1. Question and why it is binary

Will the home team win (1) or not (0: draw or away win)? Binary logistic regression is the model from Lecture 9, and Lecture 7's sensitivity, specificity, ROC and AUC apply to it directly. We also tried the three-way home/draw/away version. It is capped near 55%: on the test season even the bookmakers' favourite won only 54.4% of matches, and our multinomial model reached 52.7% (section 7).

2. Data and leakage control

  • 11 complete Premier League seasons (2014-15 to 2024-25) from Football-Data.co.uk: 4,180 matches.
  • 2014-16 only build up Elo and form history. Development data: 2016-17 to 2023-24 (2924 matches). Test: 2024-25 (366 matches).
  • Every predictor uses matches from earlier dates only. A day's results enter team history after all of that day's matches are predicted. Tests check this.
  • Matches where a team had fewer than 5 recent league games (promoted clubs' opening weeks) are excluded and logged.
  • Bookmaker odds are never model inputs. They are used only as an expert benchmark.

3. Collinearity

We started with 17 candidate predictors. gd20 = gf20 - ga20 is an exact linear combination (VIF = inf), and the shot-share variables have VIF above 100. The classic rule (drop the highest VIF until all are at most 5) also removed elo_diff, the single strongest predictor.

4. Diagnostic plots and the refinements they led to

  • Binned residuals vs elo_diff trend upward. The pruned model under-uses team strength, so we switched to target-aware VIF pruning: among VIF > 5 predictors, drop the one least related to the outcome. We also built a compact set that keeps Elo.
  • Binned residuals vs fitted probability stay inside ±2 SE, so the logit link and calibration look adequate. No polynomial terms were added.
  • Leverage / Cook's distance: the maximum Cook's D is 0.004. Some matches exceed the strict 4/n = 0.0014 screen, but all are far below the D > 0.5 to 1 level that signals undue influence. The top ten (reports/influence_top.csv) are genuine upsets, not data errors, so nothing was removed.
  • rest_diff had p = 0.999, so it was dropped from the compact model.
  • Residuals by season: 2020-21 (no crowds) is over-predicted. Hence the no_crowd indicator. Early folds cannot learn it because none of their training data is from that period.
  • Training vs validation accuracy: deeper trees fit the training data better without validating better (overfitting). Refined forests use shallow trees with large leaves.

5. 10-fold chronological cross-validation (31 configurations)

Each fold trains on all earlier matches and validates on the next block, so we never train on the future. Selection rule, declared in advance: highest pooled out-of-fold accuracy, with models within 0.25 pts treated as tied and the lower log loss winning.

Selected: logit_compact_C0.03, an L2-penalised logistic regression on 7 predictors (six have VIF 1.0-3.2; elo_diff is 5.7, slightly above 5 and below the common cutoff of 10. We kept it deliberately: the residual plots showed that dropping it hurt, and the L2 penalty stabilises the coefficient). It ties the best random forest on accuracy and beats it on log loss and AUC.

  • Gain over the baseline logistic: +3.0 pts (95% CI -2.1 to +8.1).
  • Gain over always guessing "not a home win": +6.8 pts (95% CI +0.3 to +13.5).
  • Difference from the bookmakers: -0.8 pts (95% CI -4.3 to +2.7). Our model is statistically level with the betting market.
  • The best random forest scored slightly higher on this one season. It was not selected, because the choice was locked on cross-validation before testing. Switching now would be selecting on the test set.
  • Intervals come from a paired bootstrap over match-weeks (2,000 resamples).

model accuracy macro_F1 recall_H recall_D recall_A
multinomial logistic 52.7% 0.392 82.8% 0.0% 53.1%
bookmaker favourite 54.4% 0.406 83.4% 0.0% 57.0%

Draws are about 25% of matches and are almost never the single most likely outcome, so neither the model nor the bookmakers ever predict one. This is why the three-way accuracy is so low, and why we chose the binary target.

8. Limitations

  • One test season (366 matches): roughly ±5 pts of sampling noise around any accuracy.
  • The model has no information on injuries, line-ups or transfers. The bookmakers do, which explains their small remaining edge.
  • The no-crowd indicator cannot help future predictions. It only stops 2020-21 from distorting the other coefficients.

Reproduce: python -m soccer.run --stage develop -> --stage refine -> --stage test -> python scripts/build_report.py.
